title: The Preamble (Objectives Resolution)
salient_points: Affirms that sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone and that the authority delegated to the State of Pakistan is a sacred trust. Enshrines democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance, social justice, fundamental rights, and the independence of the judiciary.
clauses: Whereas sovereignty over the entire Universe belongs to Almighty Allah alone, and the authority to be exercised by the people of Pakistan within the limits prescribed by Him is a sacred trust...
Wherein the principles of democracy, freedom, equality, tolerance and social justice, as enunciated by Islam, shall be fully observed...
Wherein the independence of the Judiciary shall be fully secured.

title: The Republic and its territories
salient_points: Declares Pakistan to be an Islamic Republic comprising four Provinces (Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Sindh), the Islamabad Capital Territory, and such states and territories as may be included in Pakistan.
clauses: (1) Pakistan shall be a Federal Republic to be known as the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, hereinafter referred to as Pakistan.

(2) The territories of Pakistan shall comprise— (a) the Provinces of Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab and Sindh; (b) the Islamabad Capital Territory; and (c) such States and territories as are or may be included in Pakistan, whether by accession or otherwise.

title: Islam to be State religion
salient_points: Establishes Islam as the official State religion of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
clauses: Islam shall be the State religion of Pakistan.

title: The Objectives Resolution to form part of substantive provisions
salient_points: Makes the substantive principles and declarations of the Objectives Resolution an active, enforceable part of the Constitution.
clauses: The principles and provisions set out in the Objectives Resolution are hereby declared to form part of the substantive provisions of the Constitution and shall have effect accordingly.

title: Elimination of exploitation
salient_points: Mandates that the State shall ensure the elimination of all forms of exploitation and the gradual fulfillment of the fundamental principle: from each according to his ability, to each according to his work.
clauses: The State shall ensure the elimination of all forms of exploitation and the gradual fulfilment of the fundamental principle, from each according to his ability to each according to his work.

title: Right of individuals to be dealt with in accordance with law, etc.
salient_points: The bedrock of the rule of law: guarantees that every citizen, and every person residing in Pakistan, has an inalienable right to enjoy the protection of law and be treated strictly in accordance with law. Prohibits state action detrimental to life, liberty, bodily integrity, or property without legal authority.
clauses: (1) To enjoy the protection of law and to be treated in accordance with law is the inalienable right of every citizen, wherever he may be, and of every other person for the time being within Pakistan.

(2) In particular— (a) no action detrimental to the life, liberty, body, reputation or property of any person shall be taken except in accordance with law; (b) no person shall be prevented from, or be hindered in, doing that which is not prohibited by law; and (c) no person shall be compelled to do that which the law does not require him to do.

title: Loyalty to State and obedience to Constitution and law
salient_points: Declares that loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen, and obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen and person within Pakistan.
clauses: (1) Loyalty to the State is the basic duty of every citizen.
(2) Obedience to the Constitution and law is the inviolable obligation of every citizen wherever he may be and of every other person for the time being within Pakistan.

title: High treason
salient_points: Defines high treason as any act that abrogates, subverts, suspends, or holds in abeyance the Constitution by use or show of force or unconstitutional means. Following the 18th Amendment, explicitly prohibits the Supreme Court or High Courts from validating any act of high treason.
clauses: (1) Any person who abrogates or subverts or suspends or holds in abeyance, or attempts or conspires to abrogate or subvert or suspend or hold in abeyance, the Constitution by use of force or show of force or by any other unconstitutional means shall be guilty of high treason.
(2) Any person aiding or abetting or collaborating the acts mentioned in clause (1) shall likewise be guilty of high treason.
(2A) An act of high treason mentioned in clause (1) or clause (2) shall not be validated by any court including the Supreme Court and a High Court.
(3) Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) shall by law provide for the punishment of persons found guilty of high treason.

title: Definition of the State
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Defines 'the State' for the purposes of Part II as the Federal Government, Parliament, Provincial Governments, Provincial Assemblies, and all local or other authorities empowered to impose taxes or cesses.
clauses: In this Part, unless the context otherwise requires, 'the State' means the Federal Government, Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament), a Provincial Government, a Provincial Assembly, and such local or other authorities in Pakistan as are by law empowered to impose any tax or cess.

title: Laws inconsistent with or in derogation of Fundamental Rights to be void
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Core judicial review anchor: declares that any law, custom, or usage having the force of law that is inconsistent with or derogates from fundamental rights is void to the extent of such inconsistency. Prohibits the State from enacting any law taking away or abridging these rights.
clauses: (1) Any law, or any custom or usage having the force of law, in so far as it is inconsistent with the rights conferred by this Chapter, shall, to the extent of such inconsistency, be void.
(2) The State shall not make any law which takes away or abridges the rights so conferred and any law made in contravention of this clause shall, to the extent of the contravention, be void.

title: Security of person
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees that no person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law. Extensively interpreted by the superior judiciary to encompass the right to clean drinking water, human dignity, public health, housing, and livelihood.
clauses: No person shall be deprived of life or liberty save in accordance with law.

title: Clean and healthy environment
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Inserted by the 26th Constitutional Amendment, 2024. Recognizes every person's fundamental right to a clean, healthy, and sustainable environment as an enforceable constitutional right.
clauses: Every person shall be entitled to a clean, healthy and sustainable environment.

title: Safeguards as to arrest and detention
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest, the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of choice, and the mandatory requirement to produce an arrested person before a magistrate within 24 hours. Regulates preventive detention review boards.
clauses: (1) No person who is arrested shall be detained in custody without being informed, as soon as may be, of the grounds for such arrest, nor shall he be denied the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of his choice.
(2) Every person who is arrested and detained in custody shall be produced before a magistrate within a period of twenty-four hours of such arrest...

title: Right to fair trial
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Inserted by the 18th Amendment, 2010. Guarantees that in the determination of his civil rights and obligations or in any criminal charge against him, a person shall be entitled to a fair trial and due process.
clauses: For the determination of his civil rights and obligations or in any criminal charge against him a person shall be entitled to a fair trial and due process.

title: Slavery, forced labour, etc. prohibited
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Prohibits slavery, trafficking in human beings, forced labor (begar), and child labor in factories, mines, or hazardous employment for children under the age of fourteen.
clauses: (1) Slavery is non-existent and forbidden and no law shall permit or facilitate its introduction into Pakistan in any form.
(2) All forms of forced labour and traffic in human beings are prohibited.
(3) No child below the age of fourteen years shall be engaged in any factory or mine or any other hazardous employment.

title: Protection against retrospective punishment
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Bars ex-post facto criminal legislation: no person can be punished for an act or omission that was not punishable by law at the time it occurred, nor subjected to a greater penalty than that prescribed at the time of the offence.
clauses: (1) No law shall authorize the punishment of a person— (a) for an act or omission that was not punishable by law at the time of the act or omission; or (b) for an offence by a penalty greater than, or of a kind different from, the penalty prescribed by law for that offence at the time the offence was committed.

title: Protection against double punishment and self-incrimination
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Prohibits double jeopardy (prosecuting or punishing a person twice for the same offence) and guarantees the privilege against self-incrimination (compelling an accused person to be a witness against himself).
clauses: No person— (a) shall be prosecuted or punished for the same offence more than once; or (b) shall, when accused of an offence, be compelled to be a witness against himself.

title: Inviolability of dignity of man, etc.
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Constitutionalizes human dignity: guarantees that the dignity of man and, subject to law, the privacy of home, shall be inviolable. Explicitly prohibits the use of torture for extracting evidence.
clauses: (1) The dignity of man and, subject to law, the privacy of home, shall be inviolable.
(2) No person shall be subjected to torture for the purpose of extracting evidence.

title: Freedom of movement, etc.
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to remain in, enter, move freely throughout, and reside and settle in any part of Pakistan, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest.
clauses: Every citizen shall have the right to remain in, and, subject to any reasonable restriction imposed by law in the public interest, enter and move freely throughout Pakistan and to reside and settle in any part thereof.

title: Freedom of assembly
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.
clauses: Every citizen shall have the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of public order.

title: Freedom of association
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to form associations or unions, and the right of every citizen not in the service of Pakistan to form or be a member of a political party. Regulates disclosure of party funding sources.
clauses: (1) Every citizen shall have the right to form associations or unions, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of sovereignty or integrity of Pakistan, public order or morality.
(2) Every citizen, not being in the service of Pakistan, shall have the right to form or be a member of a political party, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law...

title: Freedom of trade, business or profession
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation, and to conduct any lawful trade or business, subject to professional qualifications, licensing, and state monopoly regulation.
clauses: Subject to such qualifications, if any, as may be prescribed by law, every citizen shall have the right to enter upon any lawful profession or occupation, and to conduct any lawful trade or business.

title: Freedom of speech, etc.
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees freedom of speech and expression, and freedom of the press, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of the glory of Islam, integrity/security/defense of Pakistan, public order, decency, morality, or contempt of court.
clauses: Every citizen shall have the right to freedom of speech and expression, and there shall be freedom of the press, subject to any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the interest of the glory of Islam or the integrity, security or defence of Pakistan or any part thereof, friendly relations with foreign States, public order, decency or morality, or in relation to contempt of court, commission of or incitement to an offence.

title: Right to information
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Inserted by the 18th Amendment, 2010. Guarantees every citizen the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance, subject to regulation and reasonable restrictions imposed by law.
clauses: Every citizen shall have the right to have access to information in all matters of public importance subject to regulation and reasonable restrictions imposed by law.

title: Freedom to profess religion and to manage religious institutions
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to profess, practice, and propagate their religion, and guarantees every religious denomination and sect the right to establish, maintain, and manage its religious institutions.
clauses: Subject to law, public order and morality— (a) every citizen has the right to profess, practise and propagate his religion; and (b) every religious denomination and every sect thereof has the right to establish, maintain and manage its religious institutions.

title: Safeguard against taxation for purposes of any particular religion
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Prohibits compelling any person to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.
clauses: No person shall be compelled to pay any special tax the proceeds of which are to be spent on the propagation or maintenance of any religion other than his own.

title: Safeguards as to educational institutions in respect of religion, etc.
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees that no person attending an educational institution shall be required to receive religious instruction or take part in religious ceremonies relating to a religion other than his own. Prohibits religious discrimination in admissions to tax-supported institutions.
clauses: (1) No person attending any educational institution shall be required to receive religious instruction, or take part in any religious ceremony, or attend religious worship, if such instruction, ceremony or worship relates to a religion other than his own.

title: Provision as to property
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees every citizen the right to acquire, hold, and dispose of property in any part of Pakistan, subject to reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest.
clauses: Every citizen shall have the right to acquire, hold and dispose of property in any part of Pakistan, subject to the Constitution and any reasonable restrictions imposed by law in the public interest.

title: Protection of property rights
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Prohibits compulsory acquisition or taking possession of private property save by authority of law for a public purpose, and requires compensation to be fixed by law.
clauses: (1) No person shall be deprived of his property save in accordance with law.
(2) No property shall be compulsorily acquired or taken possession of save for a public purpose and save by the authority of law which provides for compensation therefor...

title: Equality of citizens
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Foundational equality clause: all citizens are equal before law and entitled to equal protection of law. Prohibits discrimination on the basis of sex alone. Authorizes affirmative action for women and children.
clauses: (1) All citizens are equal before law and are entitled to equal protection of law.
(2) There shall be no discrimination on the basis of sex.
(3) Nothing in this Article shall prevent the State from making any special provision for the protection of women and children.

title: Right to education
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Inserted by the 18th Amendment, 2010. Makes free and compulsory education for all children aged five to sixteen years an enforceable fundamental right of every child in Pakistan.
clauses: The State shall provide free and compulsory education to all children of the age of five to sixteen years in such manner as may be determined by law.

title: Non-discrimination in respect of access to public places
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees that there shall be no discrimination against any citizen on the ground only of race, religion, caste, sex, residence, or place of birth in respect of access to public places of entertainment or resort not intended for religious purposes.
clauses: In respect of access to places of public entertainment or resort, not intended for religious purposes only, there shall be no discrimination against any citizen on the ground only of race, religion, caste, sex, residence or place of birth.

title: Safeguard against discrimination in services
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Prohibits discrimination in appointments to the service of Pakistan on grounds of race, religion, caste, sex, residence, or place of birth, while constitutionalizing regional and provincial affirmative action quotas.
clauses: No citizen otherwise qualified for appointment in the service of Pakistan shall be discriminated against in respect of any such appointment on the ground only of race, religion, caste, sex, residence or place of birth...

title: Preservation of language, script and culture
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Guarantees any section of citizens having a distinct language, script, or culture the right to preserve and promote the same and, subject to law, establish institutions for that purpose.
clauses: Subject to Article 251, any section of citizens having a distinct language, script or culture shall have the right to preserve and promote the same and subject to law, establish institutions for that purpose.

title: Principles of Policy
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Establishes that it is the responsibility of each organ and authority of the State to act in accordance with the Principles of Policy, in so far as is within its capacity. Clarifies that validity of state actions cannot be questioned in court solely for non-compliance with these non-justiciable principles.
clauses: Article 29 establishes the statutory provisions governing principles of policy under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Responsibility with respect to Principles of Policy
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs state authorities to observe the Principles of Policy in all administrative and legislative actions, subject to resource availability.
clauses: Article 30 establishes the statutory provisions governing responsibility with respect to principles of policy under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Islamic way of life
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Mandates the State to take steps enabling Muslims of Pakistan to order their lives in accordance with the fundamental principles and basic concepts of Islam.
clauses: Article 31 establishes the statutory provisions governing islamic way of life under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Promotion of local Government institutions
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to encourage local government institutions composed of elected representatives of the areas concerned, with special representation for peasants, workers, and women.
clauses: Article 32 establishes the statutory provisions governing promotion of local government institutions under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Parochial and other similar prejudices to be discouraged
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to actively discourage parochial, racial, tribal, sectarian, and provincial prejudices among citizens.
clauses: Article 33 establishes the statutory provisions governing parochial and other similar prejudices to be discouraged under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Full participation of women in national life
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to take active measures to ensure the full participation of women in all spheres of national life and public affairs.
clauses: Article 34 establishes the statutory provisions governing full participation of women in national life under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Protection of family, etc.
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to protect the marriage, the family, the mother, and the child.
clauses: Article 35 establishes the statutory provisions governing protection of family, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Protection of minorities
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of minorities, including their due representation in the Federal and Provincial services.
clauses: Article 36 establishes the statutory provisions governing protection of minorities under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Promotion of social justice and eradication of social evils
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to promote educational and economic interests of backward areas, remove illiteracy, provide free secondary education, ensure inexpensive and expeditious justice, and eradicate social evils including gambling and narcotics.
clauses: Article 37 establishes the statutory provisions governing promotion of social justice and eradication of social evils under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Promotion of social and economic well-being of the people
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to secure the well-being of citizens, prevent concentration of wealth, provide social security, and eliminate Riba (usury) as early as possible.
clauses: Article 38 establishes the statutory provisions governing promotion of social and economic well-being of the people under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Participation of people in Armed Forces
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to enable people from all parts of Pakistan to participate in the Armed Forces of Pakistan.
clauses: Article 39 establishes the statutory provisions governing participation of people in armed forces under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Strengthening bonds with Muslim world and promoting international peace
part_title: Fundamental Rights and Principles of Policy
salient_points: Directs the State to preserve and strengthen fraternal relations among Muslim countries, support common interests of peoples of Asia, Africa and Latin America, and promote international peace and security.
clauses: Article 40 establishes the statutory provisions governing strengthening bonds with muslim world and promoting international peace under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The President
salient_points: Establishes the Head of State of Pakistan, representing the unity of the Republic. Sets out qualifications (Muslim, age 45+, qualified to be MNA) and election by an Electoral College consisting of Parliament and the four Provincial Assemblies.
clauses: Article 41 establishes the statutory provisions governing the president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Oath of President
salient_points: Requires the President to make before the Chief Justice of Pakistan an oath in the form set out in the Third Schedule.
clauses: Article 42 establishes the statutory provisions governing oath of president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conditions of President's office
salient_points: Bars the President from holding any office of profit in the service of Pakistan or occupying any position carrying remuneration.
clauses: Article 43 establishes the statutory provisions governing conditions of president's office under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Term of office of President
salient_points: Fixes the term of office of the President at five years, with a maximum limit of two consecutive terms.
clauses: Article 44 establishes the statutory provisions governing term of office of president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: President's power to grant pardon, etc.
salient_points: Empowers the President to grant pardon, reprieve, respite, and remit, suspend, or commute any sentence passed by any court, tribunal, or authority.
clauses: Article 45 establishes the statutory provisions governing president's power to grant pardon, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: President to be kept informed
salient_points: Obligates the Prime Minister to keep the President informed on all matters of internal and foreign policy and legislative proposals.
clauses: Article 46 establishes the statutory provisions governing president to be kept informed under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Removal or impeachment of President
salient_points: Provides the detailed constitutional procedure for the removal or impeachment of the President on grounds of physical/mental incapacity or gross misconduct, requiring a two-thirds majority of the joint sitting of Parliament.
clauses: Article 47 establishes the statutory provisions governing removal or impeachment of president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: President to act on advice, etc.
salient_points: The cornerstone of the parliamentary executive: requires the President to act strictly on and in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet or Prime Minister. Sets out referendum referral provisions.
clauses: Article 48 establishes the statutory provisions governing president to act on advice, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Chairman or Speaker to act as, or perform functions of, President
salient_points: Specifies succession rules: the Chairman of the Senate (or Speaker of the National Assembly if Chairman is unable) acts as President during a vacancy.
clauses: Article 49 establishes the statutory provisions governing chairman or speaker to act as, or perform functions of, president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament)
salient_points: Establishes Pakistan's bicameral federal legislature: Majlis-e-Shoora consists of the President and two Houses: the National Assembly and the Senate.
clauses: Article 50 establishes the statutory provisions governing majlis-e-shoora (parliament) under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: National Assembly
salient_points: Specifies the composition of the National Assembly (total seats, provincial seat allocations, women reserved seats, non-Muslim minority seats) based on official population census figures.
clauses: Article 51 establishes the statutory provisions governing national assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Duration of National Assembly
salient_points: Fixes the term of the National Assembly at five years from the day of its first meeting, unless sooner dissolved.
clauses: Article 52 establishes the statutory provisions governing duration of national assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Speaker and Deputy Speaker of National Assembly
salient_points: Provides for the election, duties, resignation, and removal of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the National Assembly.
clauses: Article 53 establishes the statutory provisions governing speaker and deputy speaker of national assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Summoning and prorogation of Majlis-e-Shoora
salient_points: Regulates the summoning, sessions, and prorogation of Parliament. Mandates a minimum of 130 working days per year for the National Assembly and establishes requisitioning powers by one-fourth of assembly membership.
clauses: Article 54 establishes the statutory provisions governing summoning and prorogation of majlis-e-shoora under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Voting in Assembly and quorum
salient_points: Establishes decision-making by majority vote (Speaker casts tie-breaking vote) and sets the quorum of the National Assembly at one-fourth of the total membership.
clauses: Article 55 establishes the statutory provisions governing voting in assembly and quorum under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Address by President
salient_points: Empowers the President to address either House or a joint sitting, and requires an annual presidential address at the commencement of each parliamentary year.
clauses: Article 56 establishes the statutory provisions governing address by president under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Rights to speak, etc., of Prime Minister, etc.
salient_points: Gives Prime Minister, Federal Ministers, Ministers of State, and the Attorney-General the right to speak and participate in proceedings of either House or joint committees (without voting rights unless an elected member of that House).
clauses: Article 57 establishes the statutory provisions governing rights to speak, etc., of prime minister, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Dissolution of National Assembly
salient_points: Regulates assembly dissolution: President dissolves the National Assembly on the binding advice of the Prime Minister (automatic dissolution after 48 hours if President fails to act). Following the 18th Amendment, Article 58(2)(b) discretionary dissolution stands completely omitted.
clauses: Article 58 establishes the statutory provisions governing dissolution of national assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The Senate
salient_points: Establishes the Senate as the permanent Upper House representing the federating units on an equal basis (equal provincial representation), ensuring subnational federal balance. Half of the members retire every three years; Senate is not subject to dissolution.
clauses: Article 59 establishes the statutory provisions governing the senate under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Chairman and Deputy Chairman
salient_points: Provides for the election of the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Senate for a three-year term following each biennial Senate reconstitution.
clauses: Article 60 establishes the statutory provisions governing chairman and deputy chairman under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Other provisions relating to Senate
salient_points: Applies National Assembly rules regarding Speaker, voting, and sessions to the Senate, and mandates at least 110 working days annually.
clauses: Article 61 establishes the statutory provisions governing other provisions relating to senate under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Qualifications for membership of Majlis-e-Shoora
salient_points: Prescribes qualifications for parliamentarians: citizenship, minimum age (25 for MNA, 30 for Senator), and moral/ethical criteria including being 'sadiq and ameen' (truthful and righteous).
clauses: Article 62 establishes the statutory provisions governing qualifications for membership of majlis-e-shoora under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Disqualifications for membership of Majlis-e-Shoora
salient_points: Comprehensive catalog of disqualifications: mental unsoundness, undischarged insolvency, holding an office of profit, loan default, conviction for moral turpitude, dual nationality, or ridiculing the judiciary/armed forces.
clauses: Article 63 establishes the statutory provisions governing disqualifications for membership of majlis-e-shoora under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Disqualification on ground of defection, etc.
salient_points: Constitutional anti-defection mechanism: a parliamentarian who resigns from their party or votes contrary to party direction in election of PM/CM, vote of confidence/no-confidence, or a Money Bill may be declared disqualified by the Party Head upon confirmation by the ECP.
clauses: Article 63A establishes the statutory provisions governing disqualification on ground of defection, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Vacation of seats
salient_points: Specifies grounds on which a member's seat becomes vacant, including written resignation or unexplained absence for 40 consecutive sitting days.
clauses: Article 64 establishes the statutory provisions governing vacation of seats under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Oath of members
salient_points: Mandates that every elected parliamentarian must take the constitutional oath set out in the Third Schedule before taking their seat.
clauses: Article 65 establishes the statutory provisions governing oath of members under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Privileges of members, etc.
salient_points: Guarantees freedom of speech in Parliament and absolute immunity from court proceedings in respect of anything said or any vote given in Parliament or any committee.
clauses: Article 66 establishes the statutory provisions governing privileges of members, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Introduction and passing of Bills
salient_points: Sets out the standard legislative procedure: a Bill with respect to any matter in the Federal Legislative List may originate in either House and is transmitted to the other House upon passage.
clauses: Article 70 establishes the statutory provisions governing introduction and passing of bills under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Mediation Committee
salient_points: Omitted by the 18th Amendment, 2010. Deadlocks are now resolved through joint sittings.
clauses: Article 71 establishes the statutory provisions governing mediation committee under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Procedure at joint sittings
salient_points: Regulates joint sittings of Parliament presided over by the Speaker of the National Assembly.
clauses: Article 72 establishes the statutory provisions governing procedure at joint sittings under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Procedure with respect to Money Bills
salient_points: Exclusive jurisdiction over the national purse: Money Bills (budget, taxes, borrowing) must originate strictly in the National Assembly. Senate provides non-binding recommendations within 14 days.
clauses: Article 73 establishes the statutory provisions governing procedure with respect to money bills under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Federal Government's consent required for financial measures
salient_points: Requires Federal Government consent before any Money Bill or financial measure affecting public revenues can be introduced by a private member.
clauses: Article 74 establishes the statutory provisions governing federal government's consent required for financial measures under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: President's assent to Bills
salient_points: Regulates presidential assent: President must assent within 10 days or return a non-money bill for reconsideration. If passed again by a joint sitting by majority of members present and voting, the President must assent within 10 days, failing which assent is deemed given.
clauses: Article 75 establishes the statutory provisions governing president's assent to bills under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Bill not to lapse on prorogation, etc.
salient_points: Provides that pending bills do not lapse by reason of the prorogation of either House, but pending bills lapse upon dissolution of the National Assembly.
clauses: Article 76 establishes the statutory provisions governing bill not to lapse on prorogation, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Tax to be levied by law only
salient_points: Fundamental rule of public finance: no tax shall be levied for the purposes of the Federation except by or under the authority of an Act of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament).
clauses: Article 77 establishes the statutory provisions governing tax to be levied by law only under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Federal Consolidated Fund and Public Account
salient_points: Defines the Federal Consolidated Fund (all revenues, loans raised, and loan repayments received by the Federal Government) and the Public Account of the Federation.
clauses: Article 78 establishes the statutory provisions governing federal consolidated fund and public account under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Custody, etc., of Federal Consolidated Fund and Public Account
salient_points: Regulates the custody, deposit, withdrawal, and accounting of moneys in the Federal Consolidated Fund.
clauses: Article 79 establishes the statutory provisions governing custody, etc., of federal consolidated fund and public account under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Annual Budget Statement
salient_points: Mandates the presentation of the Annual Budget Statement before the National Assembly showing estimated federal receipts and expenditures for the financial year.
clauses: Article 80 establishes the statutory provisions governing annual budget statement under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Expenditure charged upon Federal Consolidated Fund
salient_points: Enumerates constitutional expenditures charged directly on the Federal Consolidated Fund (remuneration of President, Judges of the Supreme Court and High Courts, Chairman/Speaker, ECP, and national debt charges), which are discussed but not voted upon.
clauses: Article 81 establishes the statutory provisions governing expenditure charged upon federal consolidated fund under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Procedure relating to Annual Budget Statement
salient_points: Distinguishes between charged expenditures (discussed, not voted) and other expenditures submitted to the National Assembly in the form of demands for grants.
clauses: Article 82 establishes the statutory provisions governing procedure relating to annual budget statement under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Authentication of schedule of authorized expenditure
salient_points: Requires the Prime Minister to authenticate the schedule of authorized expenditure following the approval of demands for grants by the National Assembly.
clauses: Article 83 establishes the statutory provisions governing authentication of schedule of authorized expenditure under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Supplementary and excess grants
salient_points: Regulates the authorization and parliamentary presentation of supplementary and excess expenditure grants during a financial year.
clauses: Article 84 establishes the statutory provisions governing supplementary and excess grants under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Votes on account
salient_points: Empowers the National Assembly to make advance expenditure grants (vote on account) pending the completion of the regular budget procedure.
clauses: Article 85 establishes the statutory provisions governing votes on account under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power to authorize expenditure when Assembly stands dissolved
salient_points: Empowers the Federal Government to authorize expenditure for up to four months when the National Assembly stands dissolved, pending the new assembly's meeting.
clauses: Article 86 establishes the statutory provisions governing power to authorize expenditure when assembly stands dissolved under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Secretariats of Majlis-e-Shoora
salient_points: Establishes separate independent secretariats for the National Assembly and the Senate, with independent recruitment and service conditions.
clauses: Article 87 establishes the statutory provisions governing secretariats of majlis-e-shoora under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Committees of Majlis-e-Shoora
salient_points: Provides for the statutory constitution of Standing Committees, Public Accounts Committees, and special committees in each House.
clauses: Article 88 establishes the statutory provisions governing committees of majlis-e-shoora under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of President to promulgate Ordinances
salient_points: Strictly circumscribes executive law-making: President can promulgate an Ordinance only when neither House is in session and immediate action is necessary. Valid for 120 days; may be extended once for 120 days by parliamentary resolution; cannot be re-promulgated.
clauses: Article 89 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of president to promulgate ordinances under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The Federal Government
salient_points: Following the 18th Amendment, vests the executive authority of the Federation in the Federal Government, consisting of the Prime Minister and the Federal Ministers, acting through the Prime Minister as chief executive.
clauses: Article 90 establishes the statutory provisions governing the federal government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The Cabinet
salient_points: Establishes the Cabinet of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister to aid and advise the President. The Cabinet is collectively responsible to the National Assembly. Governs the election and vote of confidence for the Prime Minister.
clauses: Article 91 establishes the statutory provisions governing the cabinet under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Federal Ministers and Ministers of State
salient_points: Regulates the appointment of Federal Ministers and Ministers of State from among parliamentarians; caps the size of the federal cabinet at 11% of total parliamentary strength.
clauses: Article 92 establishes the statutory provisions governing federal ministers and ministers of state under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Advisers
salient_points: Empowers the President, on the advice of the Prime Minister, to appoint not more than five Advisers with rights to speak in parliamentary debates.
clauses: Article 93 establishes the statutory provisions governing advisers under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Prime Minister continuing in office
salient_points: Authorizes the President to ask the Prime Minister to continue in office until his successor enters upon the office of Prime Minister.
clauses: Article 94 establishes the statutory provisions governing prime minister continuing in office under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Vote of no-confidence against Prime Minister
salient_points: Provides the constitutional mechanism for removing a Prime Minister: a resolution moved by at least 20% of the National Assembly members and passed by a majority of the total membership.
clauses: Article 95 establishes the statutory provisions governing vote of no-confidence against prime minister under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Vote of confidence in Prime Minister
salient_points: Repealed/Omitted.
clauses: Article 96 establishes the statutory provisions governing vote of confidence in prime minister under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Extent of executive authority of Federation
salient_points: Delineates federal executive authority to matters with respect to which Parliament has power to make laws, respecting provincial executive jurisdiction.
clauses: Article 97 establishes the statutory provisions governing extent of executive authority of federation under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conferment of functions on subordinate authorities
salient_points: Empowers Parliament by law to confer functions upon officers or authorities subordinate to the Federal Government.
clauses: Article 98 establishes the statutory provisions governing conferment of functions on subordinate authorities under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conduct of business of Federal Government
salient_points: Directs that all executive actions of the Federal Government shall be expressed to be taken in the name of the President, and regulates the Federal Rules of Business.
clauses: Article 99 establishes the statutory provisions governing conduct of business of federal government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Attorney-General for Pakistan
salient_points: Provides for the appointment by the President of a person qualified to be a Judge of the Supreme Court as Attorney-General for Pakistan, the chief legal officer of the federal state.
clauses: Article 100 establishes the statutory provisions governing attorney-general for pakistan under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Appointment of Governor
salient_points: Regulates the appointment of the Governor of each Province by the President on the binding advice of the Prime Minister. Governor must be a registered voter and resident of that Province.
clauses: Article 101 establishes the statutory provisions governing appointment of governor under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Oath of Governor
salient_points: Requires the Governor to take an oath before the Chief Justice of the respective High Court.
clauses: Article 102 establishes the statutory provisions governing oath of governor under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conditions of Governor's office
salient_points: Bars the Governor from holding any office of profit in the service of Pakistan.
clauses: Article 103 establishes the statutory provisions governing conditions of governor's office under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Speaker Provincial Assembly to act as, or perform functions of, Governor
salient_points: Provides that the Speaker of the Provincial Assembly acts as Governor during absence or vacancy.
clauses: Article 104 establishes the statutory provisions governing speaker provincial assembly to act as, or perform functions of, governor under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Governor to act on advice, etc.
salient_points: Requires the Governor to act strictly on and in accordance with the advice of the provincial Cabinet or Chief Minister. Sets out dissolution advice rules.
clauses: Article 105 establishes the statutory provisions governing governor to act on advice, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Constitution of Provincial Assemblies
salient_points: Specifies the composition and seat allocation of the four Provincial Assemblies (Balochistan, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Sindh), including general seats, women reserved seats, and non-Muslim minority seats.
clauses: Article 106 establishes the statutory provisions governing constitution of provincial assemblies under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Duration of Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Fixes the term of a Provincial Assembly at five years from the day of its first meeting.
clauses: Article 107 establishes the statutory provisions governing duration of provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Speaker and Deputy Speaker
salient_points: Provides for the election, duties, and removal of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of a Provincial Assembly.
clauses: Article 108 establishes the statutory provisions governing speaker and deputy speaker under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Summoning and prorogation of Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Regulates the summoning and prorogation of the Provincial Assembly by the Governor, and establishes the 100-day minimum annual sitting requirement.
clauses: Article 109 establishes the statutory provisions governing summoning and prorogation of provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Right of Governor to address Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Authorizes the Governor to address the Provincial Assembly.
clauses: Article 110 establishes the statutory provisions governing right of governor to address provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Right to speak in Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Gives Advocate-General of the Province and Provincial Ministers the right to participate in assembly proceedings.
clauses: Article 111 establishes the statutory provisions governing right to speak in provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Dissolution of Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Regulates assembly dissolution: Governor dissolves on the binding advice of the Chief Minister (automatic dissolution after 48 hours if Governor fails to act).
clauses: Article 112 establishes the statutory provisions governing dissolution of provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Qualifications and disqualifications for members
salient_points: Applies Articles 62 and 63 qualifications and disqualifications to members of Provincial Assemblies (MPAs).
clauses: Article 113 establishes the statutory provisions governing qualifications and disqualifications for members under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Restriction on discussion in Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Prohibits discussion in the Provincial Assembly with respect to the conduct of any Judge of the Supreme Court or of a High Court.
clauses: Article 114 establishes the statutory provisions governing restriction on discussion in provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account
salient_points: Establishes the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account of each Province.
clauses: Article 115 establishes the statutory provisions governing provincial consolidated fund and public account under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Governor's assent to Bills
salient_points: Regulates the Governor's assent to provincial legislation, return of bills, and deemed assent upon repassage.
clauses: Article 116 establishes the statutory provisions governing governor's assent to bills under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Bill not to lapse on prorogation
salient_points: Clarifies that bills pending in a Provincial Assembly do not lapse by reason of prorogation.
clauses: Article 117 establishes the statutory provisions governing bill not to lapse on prorogation under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Custody, etc., of Provincial Consolidated Fund
salient_points: Regulates custody and withdrawals from the Provincial Consolidated Fund.
clauses: Article 118 establishes the statutory provisions governing custody, etc., of provincial consolidated fund under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Annual Budget Statement (Provincial)
salient_points: Mandates the presentation of the annual provincial budget statement before each Provincial Assembly.
clauses: Article 119 establishes the statutory provisions governing annual budget statement (provincial) under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Expenditure charged upon Provincial Consolidated Fund
salient_points: Enumerates charged expenditures for provinces (Governor, High Court Judges, provincial debt charges).
clauses: Article 120 establishes the statutory provisions governing expenditure charged upon provincial consolidated fund under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Procedure relating to Annual Budget Statement
salient_points: Regulates voting and demands for grants in Provincial Assemblies.
clauses: Article 121 establishes the statutory provisions governing procedure relating to annual budget statement under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Authentication of schedule of authorized expenditure
salient_points: Requires Chief Minister to authenticate the provincial schedule of authorized expenditure.
clauses: Article 122 establishes the statutory provisions governing authentication of schedule of authorized expenditure under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Supplementary and excess grants (Provincial)
salient_points: Regulates provincial supplementary expenditure authorizations.
clauses: Article 123 establishes the statutory provisions governing supplementary and excess grants (provincial) under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Votes on account (Provincial)
salient_points: Authorizes advance provincial budget grants pending regular legislative passage.
clauses: Article 124 establishes the statutory provisions governing votes on account (provincial) under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power to authorize expenditure when Assembly is dissolved
salient_points: Authorizes provincial caretaker government spending for up to four months during assembly dissolution.
clauses: Article 125 establishes the statutory provisions governing power to authorize expenditure when assembly is dissolved under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Secretariat of Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Establishes an independent permanent secretariat for each Provincial Assembly.
clauses: Article 126 establishes the statutory provisions governing secretariat of provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Provisions relating to National Assembly to apply to Provincial Assembly
salient_points: Applies National Assembly procedural rules (voting, quorum, privileges) to Provincial Assemblies.
clauses: Article 127 establishes the statutory provisions governing provisions relating to national assembly to apply to provincial assembly under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Governor to promulgate Ordinances
salient_points: Regulates provincial ordinance-making: Governor can promulgate only when assembly is not in session; valid for 90 days; can be extended once by assembly resolution.
clauses: Article 128 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of governor to promulgate ordinances under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The Provincial Government
salient_points: Vests executive authority of the Province in the Provincial Government, consisting of the Chief Minister and Provincial Ministers, acting through the Chief Minister.
clauses: Article 129 establishes the statutory provisions governing the provincial government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: The Cabinet
salient_points: Establishes the Provincial Cabinet headed by the Chief Minister, collectively responsible to the Provincial Assembly. Regulates election of Chief Minister.
clauses: Article 130 establishes the statutory provisions governing the cabinet under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Governor to be kept informed
salient_points: Requires Chief Minister to keep the Governor informed on provincial administration and legislative proposals.
clauses: Article 131 establishes the statutory provisions governing governor to be kept informed under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Provincial Ministers
salient_points: Regulates appointment and oath of Provincial Ministers; limits cabinet size to 15 members or 11% of assembly strength.
clauses: Article 132 establishes the statutory provisions governing provincial ministers under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Chief Minister continuing in office
salient_points: Provides for the Chief Minister continuing in office during transitional vacancy until a successor assumes office.
clauses: Article 133 establishes the statutory provisions governing chief minister continuing in office under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Resignation of Chief Minister
salient_points: Omitted.
clauses: Article 134 establishes the statutory provisions governing resignation of chief minister under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Vote of no-confidence against Chief Minister
salient_points: Repealed/consolidated into Article 136.
clauses: Article 135 establishes the statutory provisions governing vote of no-confidence against chief minister under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Vote of no-confidence against Chief Minister
salient_points: Provides the constitutional mechanism for removing a Chief Minister: resolution moved by at least 20% of MPAs and passed by a majority of the total assembly membership.
clauses: Article 136 establishes the statutory provisions governing vote of no-confidence against chief minister under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Extent of executive authority of Province
salient_points: Establishes that provincial executive authority extends to all matters with respect to which the Provincial Assembly has power to make laws.
clauses: Article 137 establishes the statutory provisions governing extent of executive authority of province under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conferment of functions on subordinate authorities
salient_points: Empowers Provincial Assembly to confer statutory functions upon officers subordinate to the Provincial Government.
clauses: Article 138 establishes the statutory provisions governing conferment of functions on subordinate authorities under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Conduct of business of Provincial Government
salient_points: Directs that executive actions be expressed in the Governor's name and regulates Provincial Rules of Business.
clauses: Article 139 establishes the statutory provisions governing conduct of business of provincial government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Advocate-General for a Province
salient_points: Provides for the appointment of the Advocate-General for each Province, who serves as the principal legal adviser to the Provincial Government.
clauses: Article 140 establishes the statutory provisions governing advocate-general for a province under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Local Government
salient_points: Flagship devolution mandate inserted by the 18th Amendment: Each Province shall, by law, establish a local government system and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility and authority to the elected representatives of the local governments. Clause (2) mandates the Election Commission of Pakistan to hold local government elections.
clauses: (1) Each Province shall, by law, establish a local government system and devolve political, administrative and financial responsibility and authority to the elected representatives of the local governments.
(2) Elections to the local governments shall be held by the Election Commission of Pakistan.

title: Extent of Federal and Provincial laws
salient_points: Defines territorial legislative jurisdiction: Parliament may make laws for the whole or any part of Pakistan; a Provincial Assembly may make laws for the Province or any part thereof.
clauses: Article 141 establishes the statutory provisions governing extent of federal and provincial laws under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Subject-matter of Federal and Provincial laws
salient_points: Post-18th Amendment federal division: Parliament has exclusive power over the Federal Legislative List; Provincial Assemblies have exclusive legislative competence over all residual matters not enumerated in the Federal Legislative List.
clauses: Article 142 establishes the statutory provisions governing subject-matter of federal and provincial laws under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Inconsistency between Federal and Provincial law
salient_points: Supremacy clause: if a Provincial law is repugnant to a Federal law on a subject Parliament is competent to enact, the Federal law prevails and the Provincial law is void to the extent of repugnancy.
clauses: Article 143 establishes the statutory provisions governing inconsistency between federal and provincial law under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Majlis-e-Shoora to legislate for two or more Provinces by consent
salient_points: Authorizes Parliament to enact uniform legislation on residual provincial matters if two or more Provincial Assemblies pass resolutions requesting federal regulation.
clauses: Article 144 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of majlis-e-shoora to legislate for two or more provinces by consent under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of President to direct Governor to discharge certain functions as agent
salient_points: Authorizes the President to direct a Provincial Governor to act as presidential agent in relation to specific excluded areas.
clauses: Article 145 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of president to direct governor to discharge certain functions as agent under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Federation to confer powers, etc., on Provinces in certain cases
salient_points: Permits the Federal Government, with provincial consent, to entrust federal executive functions to a Provincial Government or its officers.
clauses: Article 146 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of federation to confer powers, etc., on provinces in certain cases under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of the Provinces to entrust functions to the Federation
salient_points: Allows a Provincial Government, with federal consent, to entrust provincial functions to the Federal Government, subject to Provincial Assembly ratification within 60 days.
clauses: Article 147 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of the provinces to entrust functions to the federation under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Obligation of Provinces and Federation
salient_points: Mandates Provinces to exercise executive authority ensuring compliance with Federal laws; obligates Federation to protect every Province against external aggression and internal disturbances.
clauses: Article 148 establishes the statutory provisions governing obligation of provinces and federation under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Directions to Provinces in certain cases
salient_points: Regulates the issuance of federal executive directions to Provinces for executing federal laws, constructing national means of communication, and preventing grave menace to peace.
clauses: Article 149 establishes the statutory provisions governing directions to provinces in certain cases under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Full faith and credit to public acts, etc.
salient_points: Mandates that full faith and credit shall be given throughout Pakistan to public acts, records, and judicial proceedings of every Province.
clauses: Article 150 establishes the statutory provisions governing full faith and credit to public acts, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Inter-Provincial trade
salient_points: Guarantees freedom of inter-provincial trade, commerce, and intercourse throughout Pakistan; prohibits provincial taxes that discriminate against goods manufactured in other provinces.
clauses: Article 151 establishes the statutory provisions governing inter-provincial trade under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Acquisition of land for Federal purposes
salient_points: Requires Provinces to acquire land at the expense of the Federation when requested for federal governmental purposes.
clauses: Article 152 establishes the statutory provisions governing acquisition of land for federal purposes under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: National Security Council
salient_points: Omitted by the 18th Amendment, 2010.
clauses: Article 152A establishes the statutory provisions governing national security council under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Council of Common Interests
salient_points: Constitutionalizes the Council of Common Interests (CCI): composed of Prime Minister, four Provincial Chief Ministers, and three Federal Ministers. Formulates and regulates policies regarding matters in Part II of the Federal Legislative List.
clauses: Article 153 establishes the statutory provisions governing council of common interests under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Functions and rules of procedure of Council of Common Interests
salient_points: Mandates that the CCI shall meet at least once in ninety days and report annually to Parliament. Decisions are by majority vote; appeals lie to a joint sitting of Parliament.
clauses: Article 154 establishes the statutory provisions governing functions and rules of procedure of council of common interests under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Complaints as to interference with water supplies
salient_points: Provides an inter-provincial dispute resolution mechanism for complaints regarding interference with natural water supplies through the Council of Common Interests.
clauses: Article 155 establishes the statutory provisions governing complaints as to interference with water supplies under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: National Economic Council
salient_points: Constitutionalizes the National Economic Council (NEC) to review the overall economic condition of the country and formulate plans for financial, commercial, and economic policies.
clauses: Article 156 establishes the statutory provisions governing national economic council under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Electricity
salient_points: Regulates federal-provincial power distribution: Federal Government must consult provincial governments before constructing hydro-electric stations; empowers provinces to construct power stations, lay transmission lines, and levy provincial electricity duty.
clauses: Article 157 establishes the statutory provisions governing electricity under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Priority of requirements of natural gas
salient_points: Crucial resource federalism clause: guarantees that the Province in which a well-head of natural gas is situated shall have priority over other parts of Pakistan in meeting its requirements.
clauses: Article 158 establishes the statutory provisions governing priority of requirements of natural gas under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Broadcasting and telecasting
salient_points: Regulates broadcasting and television transmission facilities for provincial governments.
clauses: Article 159 establishes the statutory provisions governing broadcasting and telecasting under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: National Finance Commission
salient_points: Flagship fiscal federalism provision: establishes the National Finance Commission (NFC) consisting of Federal and Provincial Finance Ministers. Crucially, Article 160(3A) establishes the non-retrogression floor rule: 'the share of the Provinces in each Award of National Finance Commission shall not be less than the share given to the Provinces in the previous Award'.
clauses: (1) Within six months of the commencing day and thereafter at intervals not exceeding five years, the President shall constitute a National Finance Commission...
(3A) The share of the Provinces in each Award of National Finance Commission shall not be less than the share given to the Provinces in the previous Award.

(4) As soon as may be after receiving the recommendations of the National Finance Commission, the President shall by Order specify... the share of the net proceeds of the taxes... which is to be allocated to each Province.

title: Natural gas and hydro-electric power
salient_points: Mandates that net proceeds of federal excise duty on natural gas, royalty on natural gas, and net profits from hydro-electric power generation shall be paid directly to the Province where the well-head or station is situated.
clauses: Article 161 establishes the statutory provisions governing natural gas and hydro-electric power under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Prior sanction of President required to Bills affecting taxation in which Provinces are interested
salient_points: Requires prior presidential sanction before introducing any federal bill that varies taxes whose proceeds are distributed to provinces.
clauses: Article 162 establishes the statutory provisions governing prior sanction of president required to bills affecting taxation in which provinces are interested under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Provincial taxes in respect of professions, etc.
salient_points: Confirms provincial legislative competence to impose taxes on professions, trades, callings, or employments.
clauses: Article 163 establishes the statutory provisions governing provincial taxes in respect of professions, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Grants out of Consolidated Fund
salient_points: Authorizes Federation or Provinces to make grants for any public purpose, even if outside their legislative competence.
clauses: Article 164 establishes the statutory provisions governing grants out of consolidated fund under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Exemption of certain public property from taxation
salient_points: Mutual tax immunity: Federal Government property and income is exempt from provincial taxation; Provincial Government property is exempt from federal taxation.
clauses: Article 165 establishes the statutory provisions governing exemption of certain public property from taxation under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Majlis-e-Shoora to impose tax on certain corporations, etc.
salient_points: Clarifies federal taxing authority over commercial corporations established by or under federal law.
clauses: Article 165A establishes the statutory provisions governing power of majlis-e-shoora to impose tax on certain corporations, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Borrowing by Federal Government
salient_points: Empowers the Federal Government to borrow money on the security of the Federal Consolidated Fund within parliamentary limits.
clauses: Article 166 establishes the statutory provisions governing borrowing by federal government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Borrowing by Provincial Government
salient_points: Empowers Provincial Governments to borrow within Pakistan; requires federal consent if prior federal loans remain outstanding. 18th Amendment inserted clause (4) permitting provinces to raise domestic and external loans under federal framework.
clauses: Article 167 establishes the statutory provisions governing borrowing by provincial government under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Auditor-General of Pakistan
salient_points: Establishes the independent Auditor-General of Pakistan (AGP) for external audit of federal and provincial public accounts. Fixed non-extendable term of four years.
clauses: Article 168 establishes the statutory provisions governing auditor-general of pakistan under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Functions and powers of Auditor-General
salient_points: Empowers AGP to audit accounts of Federation, Provinces, and statutory bodies.
clauses: Article 169 establishes the statutory provisions governing functions and powers of auditor-general under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Auditor-General to give directions as to accounts
salient_points: Empowers AGP to prescribe bookkeeping forms and directions for federal and provincial accounts.
clauses: Article 170 establishes the statutory provisions governing power of auditor-general to give directions as to accounts under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Reports of Auditor-General
salient_points: Mandates submission of AGP audit reports to the President and Governors, who lay them before Parliament and Provincial Assemblies for Public Accounts Committee (PAC) scrutiny.
clauses: Article 171 establishes the statutory provisions governing reports of auditor-general under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Ownerless property
salient_points: Regulates property accruing by escheat or bona vacantia. Crucially, Article 172(3) establishes: 'Subject to existing commitments and obligations, mineral oil and natural gas within the Province or the territorial waters adjacent thereto shall vest jointly and equally in that Province and the Federal Government'.
clauses: (1) Any property which has no rightful owner shall, if located in a Province, vest in the Government of that Province, and in every other case, in the Federal Government.
(2) All lands, minerals and other things of value within the continental shelf or underlying the ocean within the territorial waters of Pakistan shall vest in the Federal Government.

(3) Subject to existing commitments and obligations, mineral oil and natural gas within the Province or the territorial waters adjacent thereto shall vest jointly and equally in that Province and the Federal Government.

title: Power to acquire property and to make contracts, etc.
salient_points: Authorizes executive governments to acquire, hold, and dispose of property and enter into contracts.
clauses: Article 173 establishes the statutory provisions governing power to acquire property and to make contracts, etc. under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Suits and proceedings
salient_points: Establishes that the Federation of Pakistan may sue or be sued by the name of Pakistan, and a Province may sue or be sued by the name of the Province.
clauses: Article 174 establishes the statutory provisions governing suits and proceedings under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Establishment and jurisdiction of courts
salient_points: Establishes the superior judiciary: Supreme Court of Pakistan, Federal Constitutional Court (post-27th Amendment), a High Court for each Province, and the Islamabad High Court. Mandates progressive separation of the Judiciary from the Executive.
clauses: Article 175 establishes the statutory provisions governing establishment and jurisdiction of courts under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Appointment of Judges
salient_points: Constitutionalizes superior court judicial appointments: established Judicial Commission of Pakistan (JCP) and Parliamentary Committee. Restructured by the 26th and 27th Amendments to evaluate judicial performance and form Constitutional Benches.
clauses: Article 175A establishes the statutory provisions governing appointment of judges under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Constitution of Supreme Court
salient_points: Establishes the composition of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, consisting of the Chief Justice of Pakistan and such number of other Judges as determined by Act of Parliament.
clauses: Article 176 establishes the statutory provisions governing constitution of supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Appointment of Supreme Court Judges
salient_points: Prescribes qualifications for appointment to the Supreme Court: Pakistani citizenship and at least 5 years as High Court Judge or 15 years as High Court advocate.
clauses: Article 177 establishes the statutory provisions governing appointment of supreme court judges under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Oath of office
salient_points: Requires Chief Justice to make oath before President, and other Judges before the Chief Justice.
clauses: Article 178 establishes the statutory provisions governing oath of office under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Retiring age
salient_points: Fixes retirement age of Supreme Court judges at 65 years. Under the 26th Amendment, the Chief Justice of Pakistan holds a fixed term of three years (unless superannuated or resigning earlier).
clauses: Article 179 establishes the statutory provisions governing retiring age under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Acting Chief Justice
salient_points: Provides for appointment of Acting Chief Justice during vacancy or absence.
clauses: Article 180 establishes the statutory provisions governing acting chief justice under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Acting Judges
salient_points: Provides for appointment of Acting Supreme Court Judges.
clauses: Article 181 establishes the statutory provisions governing acting judges under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Appointment of ad-hoc Judges
salient_points: Regulates appointment of ad-hoc Judges when quorum of Supreme Court Judges is deficient.
clauses: Article 182 establishes the statutory provisions governing appointment of ad-hoc judges under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Seat of the Supreme Court
salient_points: Fixes the permanent seat of the Supreme Court at Islamabad, with circuit benches sitting in provincial capitals.
clauses: Article 183 establishes the statutory provisions governing seat of the supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Original Jurisdiction of Supreme Court
salient_points: Vests exclusive original jurisdiction in inter-governmental disputes. Clause (3) empowers public interest fundamental rights enforcement (suo motu), as regulated by Constitutional Benches post-26th Amendment.
clauses: Article 184 establishes the statutory provisions governing original jurisdiction of supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Appellate jurisdiction of Supreme Court
salient_points: Regulates appellate jurisdiction from High Court judgments and decrees, both as of right in specified criminal/civil matters and by leave to appeal.
clauses: Article 185 establishes the statutory provisions governing appellate jurisdiction of supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Advisory jurisdiction
salient_points: Empowers President to refer questions of law of public importance to the Supreme Court for advisory opinion.
clauses: Article 186 establishes the statutory provisions governing advisory jurisdiction under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Power of Supreme Court to transfer cases
salient_points: Empowers Supreme Court to transfer any case or appeal pending before any High Court to any other High Court or to itself.
clauses: Article 186A establishes the statutory provisions governing power of supreme court to transfer cases under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Issue and execution of processes of Supreme Court
salient_points: Empowers Supreme Court to issue directions, orders, or decrees necessary for doing complete justice in any matter pending before it.
clauses: Article 187 establishes the statutory provisions governing issue and execution of processes of supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Review of judgments of Supreme Court
salient_points: Empowers Supreme Court to review any judgment pronounced or order made by it.
clauses: Article 188 establishes the statutory provisions governing review of judgments of supreme court under the Constitution of Pakistan.

title: Decisions of Supreme Court binding on other courts
salient_points: Establishes doctrine of precedent: any decision of the Supreme Court deciding a question of law or based upon or enunciating a principle of law is binding on all other courts in Pakistan.
